candidates.rationale: Ratio of cumulative excursion above the open to excursion below it measures which side of the book is being absorbed; sustained one-sided absorption is liquidity demand paid for by dealers and reverses over the next weeks.

Counts how many days in the last two months set a fresh one-month high; repeated breakouts mark informed buyers persistently lifting offers, and anchoring at round highs makes the market underreact to that pattern, while an isolated breakout is noise.

When the upper and lower shadows co-move, both sides of the book are being hit and the move is two-sided noise; when they decouple, one side is persistently absorbing and the resulting order-flow imbalance keeps pushing price.

A floor that has risen relative to the two-month floor, scaled by the stock's own accumulated daily range, is the signature of supply withdrawal rather than a price spike, so it reads trend without being contaminated by the size of any single up day.

The share of a month's total trading range contributed by its single widest day separates a one-day shock from continuous repricing; shock-dominated names have overshot on transient liquidity and mean-revert.

Instability of the volatility itself, not its level: names whose realised vol swings around flag an unsettled information regime where quotes are widened and prices overshoot, so their moves are reversed once the regime settles.

Two-week trading width against two-month width: a collapsed ratio means disagreement has been resolved and inventory is balanced, and the market prices the persistence of volatility but not its mean reversion, so compressed names earn the subsequent expansion.

The same position in a stock's own one-month price history means continuation in a calm name and exhaustion in a turbulent one, so multiplying trend position by realised volatility separates the two regimes a plain momentum rank averages together.

Counting days that extend the prior high measures trend persistence independently of move size; profitable firms that have stopped extending are where patient buyers stepped away and price overshot down, which is the cheap side of the quality trade.

Drawdown from the quarter high expressed as the number of normal trading days of range needed to recover, counted only where the firm actually converts assets into sales; asset-efficient names that are deep in range units fell on liquidity, not fundamentals, and recover.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.


TASK: EXPLORE. Propose 10 NEW factor expressions.

Direction for this island

  (($high + $low) / 2)   (in 5 published alphas)

  ((DELAY($close, 20) - DELAY($close, 10)) / 10)   (in 3 published alphas)
  (($close - DELAY($close, 1)) * -(1))   (in 3 published alphas)

Working memory: rules written after earlier rounds on this island, oldest first. Apply them.
  1. Directional return aggregates buy almost nothing. SIGN sums, TS_MEAN/TS_STD sharpe forms, TS_ARGMAX(ABS($return),63) and summed raw OHLC gaps produced the three weakest accepts (0.382, 0.591, 0.603). Dispersion, concentration and correlation kernels produced everything above 1.9.
  2. CS_DEMEAN(CS_RANK($roe)) as a leading term is spent: in one round it drew both a 5-node archive_subtree hit and a rho 0.901 correlation hit against the same archive member. CS_ZSCORE or plain CS_RANK on $accrual_gap and $asset_turnover carried the 3.1 to 4.1 accepts.
  3. Rescaling a window is not a decorrelating edit. The 126-day channel-position kernel came back rho 0.858 against its 21-day twin. Spend mutation edits on replacing a whole leg; the one non-local reject wasted its budget scattering edits across wrapper, leg and window at once.
  4. Keep total lookback at 126 days or less. A DELAY($close,189) leg was the round's only coverage failure at 0.896; every expression at 126 or below cleared the gate, including 126-day TS_CORR.
  5. Stop spending proposals on OHLC/return-only expressions: the four price-only accepts scored 0.080, 0.297 and 0.716, while every proposal carrying a fundamental cross-sectional leg or the range-vs-volume corr scored 1.982 to 4.080.
  6. Retire the CS_DEMEAN(CS_RANK($roe)) leading leg. It produced 5 of this round's rejects (5, 7 and 14 shared nodes, one over the edit budget, and rho 0.883 when only the price leg was replaced). A plain CS_RANK($roe)/CS_ZSCORE($roa) leg still pays, but only next to a new kernel.
  7. Changing the wrapper or the field on a fundamental leg does not create distance: CS_RANK to CS_ZSCORE and $roe to $accrual_gap/$asset_turnover left the second leg whole and shared 7 and 14 nodes. Rebuild the price/volume leg instead.
  8. CS_RANK(TS_DELTA($roa, 63)) and CS_RANK(TS_DELTA($asset_turnover, 63)) are spent: three rejects shared exactly those 4 nodes with the archived MIN(...) member regardless of the surrounding operator or the other leg.
  9. Do not select 2-node archive members such as RANK($roa) as crossover parents. Three attempts all shared only 2 nodes because that is the whole parent; pick parents whose donatable subtree is at least 3 nodes.
  10. In the range-vs-volume corr, keep the volume leg a rank/level transform and the window near 42: TS_RANK($volume, 10) against $high - $low at 42 was the top accept (4.080), while TS_STD($dollar_volume, 21) at 63 screened at |t| 0.81 and $return against $high - $low at 21 only reached 0.716.
  11. Mutations that rewrote both sides of a ratio or both legs of a rank spread went 0 for 4 on locality (4 to 6 edits). Change one leg and leave the other's nodes byte-identical; a window plus one leaf is the affordable move.
  12. Two price kernels are dead ends: the overnight gap $open - DELAY($high, 1) under a rank collides with the Alpha#101 family, and $return autocorrelation TS_CORR($return, DELAY($return, 1), 21) screened at |t| 0.35.

For each proposal give a one-line economic rationale: what mechanism would make
this predict returns. "It is a momentum variant" is not a mechanism.
